sub_branches.concept: Vertically Opposite Angles and Linear Pairs
details: Two straight lines intersect at at most one unique point, forming four angles.
Vertically opposite angles are equal: angle a = angle c and angle b = angle d.
Linear pairs on a straight line are supplementary: angle a + angle b = 180°.
evidence_or_examples: If intersecting angle a = 35°, adjacent angle b = 180° - 35° = 145°, vertically opposite angle c = 35°, angle d = 145°.

details: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never meet, maintaining constant perpendicular distance throughout.
Perpendicular lines intersect at right angles (90°).
evidence_or_examples: Opposite edges of a ruler, railway tracks.

details: Successive parallel horizontal paper folds produce parallel line creases.
A perpendicular vertical fold across horizontal creases generates right angles.
evidence_or_examples: Folding square paper in half repeatedly creates parallel grid line creases.
